newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Carlos accomplice extradited to France.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Carlos accomplice extradited to France.

text.p: Italy on Thursday extradited a suspected German accomplice of notorious guerrilla Carlos the Jackal, whom French anti-terrorism investigators believe may be the key to jailing Carlos for life, justice sources said.

They said Margot Froelich, 36, wanted for questioning on two 1982 bombings in France, would arrive in Paris later on Thursday and be questioned by anti-terrorism investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere.
Bruguiere is leading several probes into bombings and attacks blamed on Carlos, whose real name is Ilich Ramirez Sanchez and who has been in a French jail since August 1994.

Froelich, arrested when she visited her husband in Rome in October 1995, is suspected of driving a car from former Yugoslavia which, after being packed with 20 kg (44 lbs) of explosives, blew up in Paris on April 22, 1982, killing a pregnant woman and injuring 63 other people.

The target of the Marbeuf Street attack was the weekly Arab newspaper, Al Watan Al Arabi, known for its critical stance towards left-wing Arab governments. But it is also thought to have been aimed at forcing the release from French jail of two other Carlos accomplices.
Files from the former East German and Hungarian secret services also link Froelich to the bombing of the Paris-Toulouse express train in March 1982, which killed five people.
Lawyers for Carlos, seized by French counter-intelligence in Sudan two years ago, have insisted he was not in France at the time of the Marbeuf Street bombing just off the Champs-Elysees.
Sources close to the probe said Bruguiere believed the woman could be vital in linking Carlos, under investigation for six attacks from 1974 to 1983, to the blast.

Justice sources said that Froelich's husband had struggled to resist the French extradition request for his wife. She had herself asked Italian authorities before travelling to Rome from Germany whether she would be arrested if she made the trip.
Italian authorities told her lawyers there was nothing pending against her in Italy but then arrested her in Rome at France's request, the sources said.
